writeup.headline: Intuitive Surgical rates Hold: strong growth and quality offset by weak trend and absolute valuation.
writeup.thesis: Intuitive Surgical scores 61, a Hold, 4 points below the Buy band. Quality is the strongest factor at 85, with a 67.2% gross margin, 28.4% operating margin, 31.1% FCF margin and diluted share count down 2.8% year on year. Growth scores 74 on TTM revenue growth of 20.4% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 21.7% year on year, with growth sped up by 3.2 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation scores 48: in absolute terms the multiples are high, at 13.3x sales and 42.8x FCF, with the FCF yield 2.7 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, though the stock is cheap against its own history (P/FCF cheaper than at 59 of the last 61 month-ends). The trend score of 38 holds the rating back, with shares down 25.2% from 12 months ago to 1 month ago and price 25.1% below its 52-week high.
key_risks: Price cuts and China pricing are expected to reduce instruments and accessories revenue per procedure by about 3–5%.
US procedure growth slowed to 10%, which could weigh on future revenue growth.
The valuation is high in absolute terms at 42.8x FCF, leaving little room for disappointment.
The $450M antitrust settlement still needs court approval, and the separate SIS case continues.
Weak relative performance, with shares 11.2 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days, and insiders selling after earnings.
what_would_change: A 4-point gain in the composite score would move the rating to Buy, for example through a recovery in the trend factor from its score of 38.
Further growth acceleration or an improving valuation score from 48 could also push the score into the Buy band.
A drop of 17 points or more would be needed for a Sell, such as a sharp slowdown in revenue growth alongside margin pressure from pricing cuts.
Clarity on the balance sheet, currently unscored, could shift the composite in either direction.
